chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from 'Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I bequeath to the present ones of my community and the absent ones from them, and those in the loins of men and the wombs of women until the Day of Resurrection, that they should maintain goodly relationships with the relatives, and even if one of them is at a travel distance of a year, for that is from the Religion.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on maintaining ties with distant relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the universality of kinship ties (silat al-rahim) by addressing the living, the absent, and future generations, highlighting its status as a core tenet of faith. The specific mention of maintaining ties even with those 'a year’s journey away' illustrates the practical extent of this obligation in Shia jurisprudence, encouraging proactive effort regardless of geographical or temporal distance.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam, 
(It has been narrated) from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> hereby bequeath the present ones of my<sup>saww</sup> community and the absent ones from them, and the ones in the backbones of the men and the wombs of the women up to the Day of Judgement that they should maintain goodly relationships with the relatives, and even if there was one from them upon a travel distance of a year, for that is from the Religion’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘I ask my followers who are present, those who are not present, those in the back of men and in the wombs of women to the Day of Judgment to maintain good relations with their relatives even though they are far away at a distance of one year’s journey; it is part of religion.’”
